newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front page - Aug 6.

text.p: The Washington Post included the following stories on the front page of its Wednesday edition:

WASHINGTON - A South Korean Boeing 747 jetliner crashed in rugged jungle terrain as it was attempting to make an early-morning landing on the South Pacific Island of Guam, apparently killing more than 200 people.
WASHINGTON - D.C. financial control board chairman Andrew Brimmer declared he is in charge of nearly the entire District of Columbia government.

WASHINGTON - Potomac Electric Power Co and RCN Corp. plan to announce a joint venture to offer Washington area consumers alternative local telephone service, high-speed Internet connections and cable television.
WASHINGTON - President Clinton signed legislation that cuts taxes for millions of Americans and puts the government on a path to a balanced budget by 2002.
SAN FRANCISCO - Attorney General Janet Reno denounced the Republican-controlled Senate for causing an "unprecedented slowdown" in confirming Clinton administration nominees to the federal bench.
KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - Many Americans are unimpressed with the balanced budget agreement, which is being hailed as a truly historic achievement.
